headline: Board elects co-chairs, vice chair, and other officer positions for the year ahead
summary: The Board for Registration of Voters elected new officers including co-chairs, vice chair, parliamentarian, and other coordinator roles. The board also amended and adopted the June meeting minutes, and discussed preparations for the August 11 state primary election and voter outreach efforts.
decisions: Elected Lesley Gendron and Lauren Ebersol as co-chairs
Elected Michelle Lefkowitz as Vice Chair, with the understanding she may decline
Elected Miriam Stoll as Outreach Coordinator
Elected Alison Harte as Volunteer Coordinator
Left the Language Access Coordinator position vacant
Elected Will Cunningham as combined Student Liaison
Elected Lesley Gendron as Resource Coordinator
Amended June minutes to reflect 2 training sessions instead of 3
Adopted the June minutes as amended

plain_text:
Board for Registration of Voters  
  
Tuesday, July 7, 2026, 6:00 PM  
 
MINUTES OF MEETING 
Police Department Community Room, 1 North Ave, Burlington, VT, 05401 OR remotely via 
Zoom. 
  
    
1. Call Meeting to Order  
  
Lesley Gendron, temporary vice chair, called the meeting to order at 6:05pm.  
 
Members in attendance: Alison Harte, Adam Franz, Colleen Montgomery, Janet Stambolian, Jeanne Keller, 
Kevin Lewis, Lauren Ebersol (remote), Karen Rowell, Lesley Gendron, Annie Schneider, Miriam Stoll, and 
Youth Member Will Cunningham 
 
Members absent: Michelle Lefkowitz 
 
Also present: Tenzin Chokden, Associate City Clerk, and Grace Grundhauser 
 
2. Agenda 
  
Motion to adopt agenda made by Alison Harte, seconded by Colleen Montgomery.   
 
3. Introductions 
  
All members introduced themselves and welcomed new member Miriam Stoll.  
 
4. Announcements 
  
No announcements besides that Miriam has joined the board. 
 
5. Meeting Length 
  
Meeting was set to end at 7pm.
6. Public Forum 
  
Motion to move Public Forum up next in the agenda made by Adam Franz, seconded by Janet Stambolian. 
Passed unanimously.  
 
Grace Grundhauser spoke about how much it meant to her to serve on the board for many years. She suggested 
that the board should nominate Lesley and Lauren to co-chair. 
 
6. Member Position Nominations 
  
Chair: Collen Montgomery nominated Lesley Gendron and Lauren Ebersol as co-chairs. Seconded by Janet 
Stambolian. Passed unanimously.  
 
Vice Chair: The board discussed nominating Michelle Lefkowitz in absentia. Colleen nominated Annie 
Schneider; Annie declined. Jeanne nominated Michelle Lefkowitz with the understanding that she may choose 
to decline to position. Seconded by Karen Rowell. Passed unanimously.  
 
Parliamentarian: Kevin Lewis nominated Adam Franz. Annie asked if Adam would continue to serve on the 
board if he is elected to the State House; Adam replied he will if it is legally permissible. Passed unanimously.  
 
Outreach Coordinator: Jeanne Keller nominated Miriam Stoll. Seconded by Janet Stambolian. Passed 
unanimously, except one abstention by Karen Rowell. 
 
Volunteer Coordinator: Janet Stambolian nominated Alison Harte. Seconded by Colleen Montgomery. Passed 
unanimously.  
 
Language Access Coordinator: The board agreed to leave this position vacant.  
 
Student Liaison: Will Cunningham suggested combining the two roles of High School Student Liaison & 
College Student Liaison into one role of Student Liaison. Adam agreed; Annie asked if Will is interested in the 
combined role. Colleen Montgomery nominated Will Cunningham. Seconded by Janet Stambolian. Passed 
unanimously.  
 
Resource Coordinator: Lesley Gendron nominated herself. Seconded by Kevin Lewis. Passed unanimously.  
 
7. Adopt Minutes 
  
7.1 Motion to adopt previous meeting’s minutes 
 
Grace Grundhauser clarified that new members should train for 2 elections, not 3 as was recorded in the June 
minutes. Colleen moved that the board should amend the minutes to reflect 2 rather than 3 training sessions. 
Passed unanimously, except one abstention from Miriam. 
 
Colleen Montgomery moved to adopt the minutes as amended. Seconded by Karen Rowell. Passed 
unanimously, except three abstentions from Miriam, Alison, and Jeanne who were not at the last meeting.  
  
8. Clerk’s Report 
  
Tenzin Chokden reported that there are 29,589 registered voters on the checklist. Out of these voters, 6,368 are 
currently challenged. In June, 115 new voters were registered, 22 voters were removed from the checklist, and 
103 voters were transferred from Burlington to other Vermont towns.
August state primary election updates as of July 2: 663 voters have been issued ballots, 71 have returned their 
ballots, and 2 returned ballots are defective. The Ward 6 polling place will still be Edmunds Elementary for the 
August primary, the only change being that all voters will enter through the front doors instead of the back 
doors. There will be Main St. parking for voters. 
 
Miriam asked how a voter is challenged. Tenzin responded that voter challenges can be triggered in several 
ways, including if a voter’s ballot is returned as undeliverable, or if property transfer records indicate a voter 
has moved. The Clerk’s Office sends out voter challenge letters to request updated information before a voter is 
removed from the checklist. Miriam and other members remarked that the current number of 6,368 seems like 
a high number of challenged voters. Tenzin replied that after the local City elections in March there were a 
number of new challenges. Lesley added that normally the Board would receive a list of challenged voters to 
approve at the meeting but not when it is so close to an election – there is a state mandated grace period before 
an election. Jeanne added that many challenges are due to change of address.  
 
9. State Primary Election Prep 
  
Annie and Lesley will be out of town for the August 11 primary. Coverage is needed in Ward 4; Kevin and 
Adam will double up to cover Ward 4. Lesley suggested conducting outreach with former board members who 
might be able to volunteer on election day. Lauren has heard back from a handful of people who can volunteer 
on different shifts.  
 
Usually there is a 2-hour training the Wednesday or Thursday evening before the election. Lesley will work to 
get the training session scheduled.  
 
Election assignments: 
Ward 1: Colleen Montgomery 
Ward 2: Lauren Ebersol 
Ward 3: Michelle Lefkowitz, Miriam Stoll (afternoon) 
Ward 4: Kevin Lewis, Adam Franz (morning) 
Ward 5: Jeanne Keller, Miriam Stoll (morning) 
Ward 6: Alison Harte 
Ward 7: Karen Rowell 
Ward 8: Janet Stambolian, Will Cunningham 
 
Tenzin is aware of and working on issues with the BRV laptops from the March election. 
 
Grace Grundhouser asked if there will be a separate local ballot or just the state ballot. Tenzin Chokden replied 
there is only a state ballot for the primary so there will be no legal resident voting. 
 
10. New Business 
  
Colleen Montgomery shared that she has been talking with Michelle at the Fletcher Free Library to secure a 
monthly tabling slot for voter registration. Anyone who is interested in tabling should share their availability. 
Lesley is curious when the library’s busy hours are.  
 
Jeanne Keller brought up the idea of working with the Department of Corrections to do voter registration 
within the Chittenden Correctional Facility. Jeanne also shared that several members of the board were tabling 
at the City Juneteenth Festival to register new voters. The board will follow up with Sarah Montgomery about a 
process for checking that voters are registered to their current address. Tenzin shared that the Clerk’s Office 
already receives new voter applications from the Chittenden Correctional Facility due to registration work from
the League of Women Voters. The group brainstormed other locations to do registration drives within 
Burlington.  
 
11. Adjournment 
  
Kevin Lewis made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Alison Harte seconded. Passed unanimously.
